questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a bigger city in the South of Europe. My host University did have interesting and relevant courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This was challenging, a lot of different websites and not a lot of information from the host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Non.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was challenging and expensive. I also faced some problems with my rent agency.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
- more expensive, 
- start early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process was very confusing. Information was limited, both about exam dates, timetables. I ended up with having overlapping courses. 
My process took time and I attended a lot of different courses in the begging, both to find the information about the courses in general and the schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked to professors from the different courses with was mostly very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded in finding classes I found interesting and relevant for my master, after a lot of time and effort.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: - don't panic, the process in Italy is more flexible and slow than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was a bit lower/less technical than my courses in Denmark, but challanging enough and very interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More discussions during classes, very involved and enthusiastic professors. We had more presentations, midterms and project work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Energy economics, 
- Environmental accounting and management, 
- Ecosystem functioning and services 
- Bioeconomy and circular economy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend Energy economics, it is a very interesting class with a good teacher and also it's not possible to have this class at University of Copenhagen. 
I also recommend environmental accounting and management, but mostly from my personal interests.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I encountered a lot of travel costs, as I wanted to explore the area around Milan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is more expensive, also general living costs are expensive in Milan compared to other European cities and other cities in Italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really know, I used Erasmus instagram to find social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Subscribe to groups for students /erasmus students in the city. Then you can find information about trips, clubs, social study events etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend to go for day trips, there is a lot of opportunities close to Milan and it is cheap to come there by train. especially hiking opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was ok-easy. The biggest difference is their time-perspective. Proffesors and students are often late.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, and say yes to join them for social events. Dont be afraid to ask them if you have questions and try to not only socialise with other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, it took some time to get use to their relationship to time, both in school and for social events.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like that they are more relaxed and enjoy the moment more than we do in Scandinavia. They often go out with friends to eat and drink. And I appreciate the culture of Aperitivo.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Use time on checking the courses before comming there. But don't stress out if you get confused as this will be more understandable when coming here. 
- Try to find courses you are interested in, and come to lectures this is a great way to get included to activities after school with local students. 
- Dont choose to challenging courses, exchange is also about having the time to get to know a different culture/people and country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Milan has a lot of different faculties, so checking where the lectures of your courses is smart, so you don't have to run between different locations of the city to get to your lectures.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was all the great people I met and got to know from all over the world. I learned a lot from getting out of my comfort zone as I didn't know anyone from before. I developed myself a lot both, academically and personally.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the feeling of not having a huge net of people around me. This was mostly a challenge in the beginning, before I got to know people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
